title: IAM Scaffolding Accelerator: Role Templates, Drift Healthchecks, and Upgrade-safe Least-Privilege Policies
creator: Aisha Ramos
description: Build a reusable Terraform module and companion automation that accelerates Private (VPC) deployments by scaffolding service roles, env-scoped role boundaries, and least-privilege policy suggestions. The module should: 1) generate opinionated role templates for common Redwood services (api-gateway, inference-worker, monitoring-agent, deployer), 2) emit well-scoped IAM policies and role boundary attachments, 3) provide upgrade-safe hooks so customers can roll policy changes with minimal disruption, and 4) surface drift and policy-health metrics via a lightweight healthcheck operator and CI gates. The goal is to reduce setup time for customers adopting Private deployments while preventing privilege creep and making upgrades auditable and reversible.
implementation_plan: 1) Define canonical role templates and role-boundary patterns (env, team, workload) as HCL module inputs. 2) Implement terraform module that outputs role ARNs, policy documents, data sources for existing principals, and optional OPA-style policy bundles for CI. 3) Add lifecycle-aware change strategy: resource tagging, stable name prefixes, and 'policy-version' variable to enable canary rollouts. 4) Build a small healthcheck Lambda/sidecar (container) that periodically validates IAM bindings against a 'desired state' datafile and emits metrics to CloudWatch/Datadog. 5) Integrate OPA policy tests into repo CI with terraform plan hooks and a policy-test stage. 6) Document migration path and provide an upgrade playbook with rollback steps and a canary schedule.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes inputs for environment (dev/stage/prod), workload tags, role templates, and policy_version
Module produces stable role names/ARNs and optional role boundaries for environment scoping
Policy changes can be toggled via policy_version with documented canary rollout steps
CI includes OPA-based policy unit tests that block merges on high-risk privilege additions
Healthcheck component runs and reports drift detection metrics and a remediation suggestion field
Integration test: create a fresh VPC private deploy using the module, run the healthcheck, and verify no high-severity findings
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with PM (Priya Nair) and Security (Ethan Walker). Agreed scope: role templates for four core workloads, OPA tests in pipeline, and simple healthcheck with Datadog metrics.

2026-02-27: Prototype HCL template for api-gateway and inference-worker roles completed (branch: feat/iam-templates). Early review: remove wildcard S3 write on inference-worker; replace with explicit bucket ARNs.
2026-03-03: Security review checkpoint — accepted role boundary approach but requested explicit documentation for cross-account assumption steps.
2026-03-07: Implemented terraform outputs and policy_version variable. Added terraform plan CI hook (pre-merge) that uploads plan and OPA test results to build artifacts.

2026-03-10: Healthcheck PoC deployed to a staging account. Detects drift when a test user is granted extra policies; emits metric 'iam.drift.count' and writes a remediation suggestion to SSM parameter store.
2026-03-10: Next: add automated migration example for customers with pre-existing roles and coordinate canary schedule with infra team. Assigned follow-ups to ENG-758215 and ENG-758216.
risks: Mis-specified role boundaries could block legitimate cross-account access; require staging validation
Automated policy upgrades could cause service disruption if a role ARN changes — mitigate with stable naming and canary policy_version
Drift detector false positives if out-of-band automation is not modeled; include ignore-list and tagging heuristics
qa_plan: Unit test: terraform validate + kitchen-terraform smoke for each role template
Integration: apply module in a disposable staging account and run healthcheck; verify metrics and SSM remediation note
CI gate: OPA policy tests must pass before terraform plan is allowed to be merged
Chaos test: simulate a wrongful policy attachment and ensure healthcheck detects and alerts within 5 minutes
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module behind feature flag (module variable): enabled=false by default. 2) Run automated onboarding for two internal pilot teams (infra & platform) for one week under monitoring. 3) Enable canary policy_version for 10% of deployments (pilot projects). 4) After 2 successful weeks with zero high-severity drift alerts, enable default for new private-deploys. 5) Offer migration playbook and 'safe-migrate' script for customers with pre-existing roles.
notes: Don't conflate 'role boundary' with organization-wide SCPs — boundaries are recommended for workload scoping
Provide an 'override' path for legacy customers but require an SLA ticket for manual review
Consider generating a migration report that enumerates gaps between existing policies and computed least-privilege recommendations
